correctness.rationale: For any spanning tree, deletion of e admits exactly c_T(e) crossing replacement edges and exactly one of them returns T. Detailed balance follows from sharing the same cut forest in a one-edge exchange. On K_{2,b}, degree sums force one degree-two B vertex, b-1 leaves and two bridge edges; the crossing counts are exactly 2 and b, giving the state-independent marked four-cell law. Conditional constancy inductively proves iid marks for every initial tree. On K_{a,b} with both parts at least three, direct computation on a double star and zigzag gives a strictly positive Q gap, and stationary two-step holding covariance equals Var_pi Q>0. The algebraic increment has sign b-4. The packaged independent rational checker passes 2345 assertions over finite examples.

originality.rationale: The new statement classifies independence of the entire sequence of unchanged-update indicators on all complete bicliques. The key additional comparisons are two explicit nonisomorphic current trees at width at least three and the uniform four-cell marked step law at width two. The exact insert-first Markov kernel of Dias et al. is different; static and independently sampled spanning-tree results do not imply this conditional sequential classification. value.rationale: The main result is a natural complete structural classification of update-clock independence over all bicliques, not a special-case probability. It distinguishes an exactly binomial, geometrically thinned change clock at bipartition width two from positive serial holding correlation at width three and beyond. The sharp integer minimizers give actionable finite-size calibration for attempted versus effective tree exchanges, and the four-cell marked law provides exact trajectories for every starting tree. This is motivated by the statistical behavior of a well-defined spanning-tree MCMC kernel; no general mixing result is asserted.
